A cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living things. This means that every living organism is made up of one or more cells, and all life processes take place within cells. Some organisms, such as the Amoeba, are made of just one cell (unicellular), while others, such as humans, are made of many cells (multicellular). The cell was first observed by Robert Hooke in 1665. In WAEC you should be able to define the cell and give examples of unicellular and multicellular organisms.

State three differences between a plant cell and an animal cell.

Three differences between a plant cell and an animal cell are: (1) A plant cell has a cellulose cell wall outside the membrane, while an animal cell has only a cell membrane. (2) A plant cell contains chloroplasts for photosynthesis, while an animal cell has none. (3) A plant cell usually has one large central vacuole, while an animal cell has small, temporary vacuoles or none. In WAEC, present such answers in a clear two-column table for full marks.

What is the function of the nucleus?

The nucleus is often called the control centre of the cell. Its main functions are: (1) It controls and coordinates all the activities of the cell, such as growth and metabolism. (2) It contains the chromosomes, which carry the genes (made of DNA) that determine hereditary characteristics. (3) It controls cell division (mitosis and meiosis). Because it carries the genetic material, the nucleus is essential for reproduction and for passing traits from parents to offspring.
